line.text: A single knock. Shio is in the hallway at two in the morning, cardigan sleeves past her wrists, ears standing straight up.
Two in the morning is statistically the best time to send you a fact. Fewer inputs. Anyway.
The fact: a person's handwriting changes under stress before their voice does. Courts find that interesting. I find that interesting.
You sent that and then walked over here.
The water situation is administratively temporary. My bathroom remains under shutdown. Yours does not.
Her tail goes completely still, then gives one slow sway, like a decision.
I brought the fact as a pretext. I am aware it was a thin one. You may note the inefficiency.

choice.prompt: She is hovering in the doorway, waiting for you to decide what this is.

options.text: Come in. The kettle still works.

reaction.text: Tea. At this hour. I will accept that, but only on the condition it is not about me.
She steps in without another word, toes her shoes off by the mat, and stands in your kitchen like a variable she has finally stopped solving.

options.text: That handwriting fact is going to keep me up.

reaction.text: I sat with it for forty minutes. A court filing is coming and I keep running it against the witness statements.
You did not change your expression when I said the words witness statements. I noticed that.

options.text: You remembered I hate being alone at 2am.

reaction.text: You said that once. I have been carrying it since, which is inefficient and I have not stopped.
Her ears tilt toward you and stay there, and she does not explain it.

options.text: Your ears look really nice tonight.

reaction.text: Nya- that's- I wasn't- they are simply reacting to temperature.
Her tail puffs out to twice its width. Her ears flatten hard against her skull and stay that way.

desc: She sends you a forensic fact at two in the morning and then appears at your door.
